direction: Modify one effective coefficient without changing common scaling.
hypothesis: Adjusting a term that actually changes ranking is more informative than changing a positive common divisor.

operations.mechanism: Preserve nearest start and the unnormalized equivalent of the winner. Change only the demand-dependent distance coefficient; leave the main savings and proximity weights intact.

preserve: Keep deterministic feasible customer selection, read-only inputs and the fixed evaluator.

research_activity.finding_summary: The winner improved to 11.31618. Its in-route divisor is the current node's depot distance, common to all candidates, so it cancels in the ranking; the effective changes are the distance and demand coefficients.
